scope: Verificação documental, não teste de compatibilidade ou desempenho.

claims: Terrain3D v1.0.2-stable documents that its foliage MultiMesh instances do not automatically create physics collisions and that complex multi-mesh objects require preparation or another placement method.

The current official ProtonScatter listing labels the addon MIT and unstable; its author's README states that most demo textures were made from Textures.com images with separate redistribution conditions. It should not be described as tested in this project's Godot 4.7.

evidence.text: Source https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TokisanGames/Terrain3D/v1.0.2-stable/doc/docs/instancer.md : Simple Objects says MultiMesh supports one mesh and suggests combining complex objects or another placement tool. No Collision says GPU-rendered instances are unknown to CPU physics, recommends grass or objects not needing collision, and describes instance collision as a future possibility.

Source https://store.godotengine.org/asset/hungryproton/protonscatter/ checked 2026-11-14: Changelog version 4.2.0; licence MIT; minimum Godot 4.4; publisher marked version unstable. These data do not assert testing in Godot 4.7.

Source https://github.com/HungryProton/scatter README License: addon MIT; demo 3D assets MIT; most bundled demo textures created using Textures.com images; prohibits redistributing those textures standalone and allows use as part of a larger project subject to source terms.
